predecessors.name: Electorate of Hanover
predecessors.text: the Hanoverian electorate, which Cliopatria continues as its 'Kingdom of Hanover' row from 1803

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: 'Annexed by Prussia: 20 September 1866' (infobox); it became the Prussian Province of Hanover

ledger.x: 1803: the Hanoverian realm enters Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Hanover' row, the electorate under George III, conquered that year by the French.
1807: the Hanoverian south is merged into the new Kingdom of Westphalia.
1810: the rest of the Hanoverian realm is annexed by Westphalia and France.
December 1810: the north is annexed by France.
December 1810: the French occupation of the north ends in annexation, drawn as the French empire's land (previous event).
26 October 1813: Westphalia falls and Hanover is restored.
October 1813: the Hanoverian north is freed from France.
12 October 1814: the Electorate of Hanover is constituted as a kingdom.
9 June 1815: Hanover gains East Frisia from Prussia.
1815: Hildesheim, Lingen, northern Münster and Bentheim join the kingdom.
15 June 1866: the Prussian army invades Hanover.
About 29 June 1866: the Hanoverian army surrenders.
20 September 1866: the Kingdom of Hanover ends; its land becomes the Prussian Province of Hanover.

wars.name: French occupation of Hanover (1803)
wars.outcome: The Convention of Artlenburg (5 July 1803) 'disbanded the Electorate of Hanover and instigated its occupation by French troops'.

wars.name: Napoleonic annexations of Hanover (1807-1813)
wars.outcome: Hanover is merged into the Kingdom of Westphalia (1807), the north annexed to France (December 1810); the status quo of 1806 is restored on 26 October 1813.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Hanover beats the Prussians at Langensalza (27 June 1866) but surrenders; 'Prussia annexes Hanover, Holstein, Schleswig, Hesse-Kassel, Nassau, Frankfurt'; the German Confederation is dissolved by the Peace of Prague (23 August 1866).

certainty.note: Occupation and annexation by the French, Westphalians and (per the electorate dossier) Prussians; the pages name units, not boundary lines.
Treaty borders from the Final Act of 9 June 1815 and the German Confederation; the Lauenburg and East Frisian frontiers are the treaty lines.
